title: Oral Ulcer Differential Algorithm
subtitle: Trauma, aphthae, HSV, Behcet, bullous disease, LP, and malignancy

steps.prompt: Solitary persistent ulcer >2-3 weeks, indurated border, tobacco risk, or unexplained bleeding?
Biopsy / oral medicine or ENT pathway
Recurrent round shallow ulcers on nonkeratinized mucosa without systemic signs?
Grouped vesicles/erosions, keratinized mucosa, fever, or recurrence at same site?
Genital ulcers, eye disease, GI symptoms, target lesions, skin blisters, or reticular white striae?
Behcet, IBD, EM/SJS, pemphigus/pemphigoid, or erosive LP pathway
Trauma, medication, nutritional deficiency, xerostomia, or culture/biopsy if persistent

citations.quote: StatPearls Recurrent Aphthous Stomatitis review summarizes morphology, recurrence, and systemic associations.
StatPearls Oral Mucosal Lesions review discusses infectious, inflammatory, autoimmune, traumatic, and neoplastic causes.
